summary: CONTRACT_M6 2.8 done in Editor/LevelAudit.cs, plus three fixtures. All 22 self-test fixtures pass. On levels 1 to 17 the only schedule failures are the known ones: level 10 (rock lesson), 13 and 17 (loiter rule). Levels without the new features produce the same search, keys and tables as before. BRIEF FOR THE LEVELS AGENT. (1) WARDROBE. The prop is kind "wardrobe", 1.0 x 2.0 x 0.6 m, an occluder. Its front is the prop's yaw forward (local +z). Only a body that fits can hide (WardrobeRule.Fits: the stool or the floor lamp), and the audit never hides a furniture carrying a load. Hide cells are walkable cells whose centre stays in WardrobeRule.InFront at every 0.1 m release offset: 0 to 0.6 m ahead of the front face and within 0.5 m sideways. With the stool, put the front face 0.35 to 0.45 m from a row of cell centres. The map marks hide cells 'A' and a note lists them. A closed, unopened leaf in reach of the cell blocks the hide, because E opens the door first. Entering and leaving each take 0.5 s, seen as moving, with no noise. While hidden the furniture is unseen, silent and still. The creak gauge keeps filling. A creak is muffled to 3.5 m and allowed only if nobody is inside that radius over its whole 3 s window. Hiding counts as waiting, so the 8 s wait cap and the loiter rule still apply: keep a hide (both actions included) to about 6 to 7 s. While hidden, a human who sees the remembered spot (the spawn, or the seat home after a sit) is refused, as is a sitter who forces the player. So keep the spawn out of every human's view during the hide: test_m6_audit_wardrobe uses a start room the watcher cannot see. The furniture comes out where it went in. Routes get the actions "hide" and "leave" (LevelAudit.RouteHide and RouteLeave). Lesson "wardrobe" means: no schedule with hiding off and no wait cap. Watch the wardrobe's shadow: cells it hides from a watcher are free hiding spots, so fill them with an OCCLUDER prop (a prop with occluder false has no collider and blocks nothing). (2) DOORS OPENED BY INHABITANTS. Set "openedByInhabitants": true on a closed leaf. The audit replays GameState.StepHouseholdDoors on the stepped walks (WalkReachesLeaf, then a 0.6 s Hold): the leaf swings from the hold's step for 0.6 s, and a note gives the window ('porte X ouverte par Y : peut-etre en train de s'ouvrir de a s a b s'). During that window sight takes both leaf poses. Cells within (door width + body half-diagonal + 0.1 m) of the hinge are forbidden from the window minus 0.3 s to the window plus 0.3 s. After the window the leaf is open for good, in every table and every move. The player never opens a leaf that a walk reaches. A leaf no walk reaches in 300 s stays an ordinary closed leaf, and a note says so. Station walks and the walk check use these doorways. The validator refuses stations inside a leaf's swing sector. (3) DOOR MEMORY ("doorMemory": true). Conservative rule: a leaf the player opened must never be seen standing open by any human (they all remember the authored states), from the start of its opening until the exit, using the 4 open-pose samples with 0.3 s dilation. The put back is not modelled. A leaf the household opens is remembered open by everyone, so it adds no constraint. In practice the player opens a door no human looks at before the exit, or reaches the exit before the next glance. Full audit (flags off): every level except 7 fails the material budget (level 1 went from 21 to 25 materials, same slots and renderers as the M5 log). That comes from the M6 texture or cone-outline materials, not from the audit.
